description: Signal-Server is an open-source radio-frequency propagation engine that computes point-to-point path loss and area coverage for transmitters, derived from SPLAT! 1.3 and extended for multi-threaded server use with several propagation models (among them ITM/Longley-Rice, ITWOM, Hata, COST231, SUI, ECC33, Ericsson and free-space), high-resolution terrain and land-cover clutter. It was developed from 2011 by Alex Farrant to power the RFSignal app, which became the commercial CloudRF service; CloudRF maintained it until 2023 and now keeps the repository only as history, pointing users to community forks such as W3AXL/Signal-Server (updated 2025). Coverage: anywhere with SRTM or other elevation tiles, at the resolution of the terrain data (down to 1 arc-second or finer LIDAR). Format and access: C++ source built with CMake on Linux, run from the command line with parameters for antenna, frequency and model; free of charge under the GNU GPL version 2. Caveats: the original repository is unmaintained and forks vary in quality; results depend on terrain and clutter inputs; no graphical interface. Simulation uses: coverage and hazard exposure analysis of mobile, broadcast and emergency radio networks, capacity planning of new sites, and resilience assessment when sites fail. Related records: forked from SPLAT!, uses the NTIA Irregular Terrain Model among others, and can be fed with OpenCelliD or regulator transmitter locations.
